studies.label: TRIZ-C+LLM vs TRIZ-C experiment on three engineering problems (GT, MB, WT)

arms.name: TRIZ-C+LLM
arms.description: TRIZ contradiction matrix with an LLM assistant and a prompt pack covering problem framing, contradiction parameters, inventive principles, solution generation, and a diversity check. Microsoft Copilot with Smart GPT-5 was recommended; other assistants were permitted if reported (PDF p. 5, printed p. 511, Section 3.3).

arms.name: TRIZ-C
arms.description: TRIZ contradiction matrix only, with access to triz40.com and instructions not to use any LLM-based AI assistants (PDF p. 5, printed p. 511, Section 3.3).

studies.task: Each engineering student individually generated, selected, developed, and documented a concept for a polymer gear testing rig, a bicycle drive mounting bracket, or wind turbine power maximization using the assigned TRIZ method.

ai_tool.name: Microsoft Copilot with the LLM option Smart GPT-5 (recommended; other LLM-based AI assistants allowed)

estimates.outcome: Design quality (expert-rated composite), full-sample Method main effect
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Experts holding PhDs in mechanical engineering rated feasibility, fulfillment of technical requirements, innovativeness, and elaboration on a seven-point scale; design quality is the average of these criteria. Two experts independently rated GT and MB solutions, with their ratings averaged per criterion; another independent expert rated WT solutions. Each student contributed one final solution. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 510), Section 3.2.2; PDF p. 5 (printed p. 511), Section 3.2.2 continuation. Blinding and inter-rater agreement are not reported.

sources.quote: Regarding the main effect of the Method factor, the following values were obtained: F(1, 108) = 3.21, p = .076, which is not significant.

sources.locator: PDF p. 6 (printed p. 512), Table 2, Total block; unparenthesized N values are design-quality counts

estimates.notes: This is the full-sample Method main effect from the two-way ANOVA, following the reconciled screening form. Table 2 Total rows are descriptive arm means that pool different proportions of the problem groups; they are not the marginal means for this Method test. They therefore do not populate the mean or SD fields, and no separate effect is calculated from them. The paper does not print the marginal arm means, a signed Method difference, its SE or CI, or a standardized effect. The F test alone does not identify a signed effect. se_basis is participant because the ANOVA uses a single expert-rated final-solution composite for each randomized student, averaging raters before analysis where applicable. The authors note unequal variances and potentially liberal F tests. Design quality is the outcome of RQ1 (PDF p. 2, printed p. 508); no preregistration is stated. The construct follows the screening decision of usefulness: it is a design-quality composite containing feasibility and requirements as well as innovativeness and elaboration. Both arms use TRIZ, so the added LLM is compared with the shared usual TRIZ procedure. Table 2 parenthesized values concern student satisfaction and are not used as output scores or design-quality counts.

open_items: For the full-sample ANOVA Method effect, the paper does not print marginal arm means, a signed difference, a compatible standardizer, an SE, a confidence interval, or a standardized effect. The Table 2 Total means and SDs do not identify this contrast. These fields remain null; no quantities were derived from the F statistic.

The total randomized count and the arm assignment or timing of the excluded GT student are not reported. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 510), Table 1 note. Analysis counts come directly from Table 2, not degrees of freedom.

The assistants actually used by students and their release years are not reported. Copilot with Smart GPT-5 was recommended but alternatives were permitted. ai_tool.year remains null. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 511), Section 3.3.

Study countries and the randomization procedure are not stated. The numbered locations in Figure 2 do not identify countries, and author affiliations are not treated as study locations. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 510), Section 3.2.1 and Figure 2.
Separate statistics for innovativeness or the other design-quality components, rater blinding, and inter-rater agreement are not reported. PDF pp. 4–5 (printed pp. 510–511), Section 3.2.2.

The screening form leaves partitioning of the problem groups into samples open. This extraction retains its S1 definition and the joint full-sample Method test. Treating problem groups as separate studies would require reconsidering the WT result; GT and MB do not individually meet the codebook sample-size threshold.
Data and materials are available only from the corresponding author upon reasonable request; no public data or supplement link is printed. PDF p. 9 (printed p. 515), Data availability.
notes: Extraction date: 2026-10-10; extractor A. The complete markdown conversion, including references, and all PDF pages were read; there is no appendix or supplement in the document. Figure 4 was also inspected in memory to check the survey-outcome labels. S1 follows the screening form as one individually randomized experiment analyzed jointly across problem groups. lab_rct follows the common test protocol, although GT and MB were embedded in coursework (PDF pp. 4–5, printed pp. 510–511). The problem groups differ in background and prompting experience, so problem differences cannot isolate difficulty from group characteristics (PDF p. 8, printed p. 514). No across-people or after-AI output outcome is reported. The PDF text layer encodes the printed plus sign in TRIZ-C+LLM as U+0001 in prose and tables; arm names and the copied count quote render this as a plus sign, consistent with the printed arm name in Figures 2 and 4. Whitespace in source quotes is collapsed; numeric content is unchanged. No derived effect sizes, marginal means, standard deviations, counts, or model release years have been added.
